question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]?$

current_example.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry $a_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term $a_{ij}x_i x_j$ in the expression of the quadratic form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =-1{x}_{1}{x}_{1}+(1){x}_{1}{x}_{2}+(1){x}_{2}{x}_{1}+-1{x}_{2}{x}_{2} \\  & =-{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a quadratic form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2})+{x}_{2}({x}_{1}-{x}_{2}) \\  & =-{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
